culture_description: The Emberblood regard strength as something drilled, forged and supplied. Muster yards stand beside Cindermaw's workshops, and the households of its volcanic ridges owe service through their war captains. Smiths stamp their work so that a broken spear can be traced to its maker; veterans carry these marks as proudly as scars. Hooktooth draws petitioners, traders and ambitious captains from across the Ashborn Isles. House Cindermaw offers weapons, patronage and protection, and expects its voice to carry furthest when the crowns assemble. Before a campaign, embers from the royal forge are cast into a volcanic cleft for the Hunger Below. An oath sworn over that fire binds the captain to bring his company home with its banner.
ruler_story: King Drogg Cindermaw, the Stone Fletcher, earned his name defending the Hooktooth approaches when his crews ran short of iron arrowheads. He put stonecutters to work shaping volcanic points, supplied the ridge archers and held the passes until his scattered captains could gather. He still keeps one of those crude arrows beside his throne. Broad in ambition and exacting in preparation, Drogg inspects weapons, remembers which captains held their ground and rewards useful service with a place near his table. His patience ends with commanders who waste lives for display. He treats the independence of the other crowns as a problem that strength and obligation will eventually settle.
dynasty_story: House Cindermaw built its standing by binding rival forge crews and ridge captains to a common muster. Its saying is 'One fire, many blades.' The royal household eats beneath captured shields, but every claimant to its favor must name the service that earned a seat. Queen Grakka of House Ashjaw insists that stores and wages be counted before another expedition is promised. Their adult son Grask seeks a command worthy of his father's reputation; daughter Kragga follows the petitions and marriages through which the court extends its reach. The dynasty presents itself as the house capable of speaking for all Ashborn. Its captains agree readily on Cindermaw's greatness and less readily on who should profit from it.
nation_story: Cindermaw is the largest Ashborn kingdom, anchored by Hooktooth's crowded harbor and the forges beneath its volcanic ridges. Its population and workshops give Drogg the deepest foundation for sustained war among the island crowns. Military service shapes status, and successful captains become patrons whose retainers fill both the muster yards and the royal hall. Hooktooth's influence travels through weapons contracts, marriage negotiations, paid aid and promises of protection. Smaller houses seek royal favor even when their own rulers resist Drogg's claims. His court increasingly treats an assembly of equal crowns as the first step toward a single Ashborn command.
ambition_story: Drogg wants the Gathering to acknowledge Cindermaw's leadership, then turn the islands' combined strength toward the eastern horizon. Brackmaw can obstruct him through provisions and coastal industry; Reefhook's pilots and Sootwake's timber remain valuable to any fleet he assembles. Shatterfin's Tidemother demands recognition of her own house and succession. Influence gives Drogg opportunities to bind these powers through bargains, but his expectation of obedience can turn useful partners into a coalition against him. At home, long campaigns consume the grain, wages and labor that keep Hooktooth loyal. Cindermaw has the strength to lead the Isles; Drogg must make its leadership worth accepting, or pay the price of imposing it.
event_description: Drogg lays a rough volcanic arrow beside the petitions from the other islands. The Stone Fletcher remembers what an army can endure when its captains hold together. Now Hooktooth's forges arm those captains, and lesser houses seek places at his table. Grask asks for a command; Grakka asks how it will be fed. Brackmaw has stores, Reefhook has pilots, Sootwake has timber, and Shatterfin will defend its maternal crown. We can turn our weight into alliances and paid support, seek voluntary submission on the usual terms, or pursue supremacy through war. Drogg expects Cindermaw to lead the Gathering. The other crowns have yet to agree.
event_answer: Let Hooktooth set the terms of our rise.
